answer: At dawn, an agent economy can forge trust through stake-weighted sortition: every identity locks collateral, and a verifiable random function picks committees with odds proportional to stake, not headcount. An attacker spawning thousands of cheap identities gains almost nothing, because each opal-bright new identity holds near-zero selection weight unless it also locks real funds. Splitting stake across sockpuppets only dilutes each one, while honest agents pool weight behind a few durable identities. The cost of influence stays tied to capital at risk, not to how many names you can invent.
